headline: Deep learning models for peptide design and binding prediction face generalization tests
label: Deep Learning Biomolecular Modeling
summary: Recent preprints and publications apply protein language models, diffusion, and co-folding to peptide design, binding affinity, and conformation selection.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned sequence and structure models for biomolecular binding and design, increasingly tested for where they fail. Several items focus on evaluation: GRIMM clusters enzyme sequences by similarity to stratify its function benchmark, UnbiasNet uses entity-balanced evaluation to remove degree ratio shortcuts in multi-input association prediction, and a structure-based TCR-pMHC study assesses generalization to unseen peptides. Co-folding comparisons show that ligand input format and charge alter predictions from AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, Chai-1, and Protenix-v1. On the generative side, DiffuNovo, ProtFlow, BOND-PEP, and PocketXMol produce peptides or small molecules under added constraints such as precursor mass, flow-based semantic distribution learning, or topology conditioning. What is new is the pairing of generative design with explicit control of evaluation confounds. Not every item shares this emphasis; the binding-affinity datasets and GPCR interactome work emphasize scale and coverage.
